verdict: STS DENIAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND — ROLE NAME MISMATCH ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeployApply

rootCause.detail: The approved Cursor OIDC trust and inline policy were applied to a role named ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeployApply (the intended inline policy name). Cursor OIDC can assume that role. sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity against the bucket-lock name ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeploy remains AccessDenied.

ruledOut.oidcProvider: Same api.cursor.com provider and user:325724407 token assume staging and the Apply-named role
ruledOut.sessionDuration: 900s and 3600s fail on the requested name; success on the Apply-named role with 900s
ruledOut.permissionsBoundary: Not implicated; assume of the Apply-named role succeeded
ruledOut.scp: Not required to explain the split: one role in-account is assumable, the requested name is not

smallestCorrection: Create IAM role exactly named ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeploy (IAM cannot rename).
Copy the same approved trust JSON and the same inline policy ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeployApply onto that exact role name.
Do not change the production S3 deny-except-ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeploy bucket policy.
Do not deploy using ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeployApply; the bucket lock will deny it.
After the correctly named role assumes, delete ChecksOpsProductionSpaDeployApply so there is not a second production deploy role.
